topics.title: Saccade product and execution boundary
topics.summary: The sources agree that Saccade is a semantic Truth Layer with one Extension-to-MCP route, but conflict on whether all execution is external or Registry-bounded object-addressed software execution is part of core Saccade. This must not be auto-published until the owner resolves the stale external-only wording.
topics.currentMarkdown:
# Product and execution boundary

- R-001 — Saccade is a model-independent live semantic Truth Layer for authorized Chrome and Edge tabs.
- R-002 — The production route is Extension → Native Messaging Host → owner-only local IPC → MCP.
- R-003 — Playwright, CDP, screenshots, selectors, and arbitrary coordinates are not product fallback routes.
- R-004 — Unresolved: older contributor guidance says execution is entirely Agent-owned, while current architecture permits Registry-approved object-addressed software click, select, and type through `saccade.act`.
- R-005 — The optional Reference Actuator remains development-only and is not a default product dependency.

changes.reason: The execution-owner statements are materially inconsistent and require an owner decision rather than date-based selection.

topics.title: Browser Truth observation contract
topics.summary: The architecture, decisions, and Extension contract consistently define one full semantic document view followed by pushed revision-bounded deltas, stable document-local object identity, current CSS-pixel geometry, protected-value redaction, and explicit opaque or restricted boundaries.
topics.currentMarkdown:
# Browser Truth observation contract

- R-001 — The Extension compiles each authorized tab into one canonical full semantic view and then pushes meaningful revision-bounded deltas.
- R-002 — Objects have stable document-local identity, bounded semantic state, affordances, current document- and viewport-relative CSS-pixel geometry, and explicit limitations.
- R-003 — Geometry changes update the same object identity; document replacement creates a new document boundary and invalidates stale authority.
- R-004 — Editable values, protected values, cookies, storage, DOM paths, and locators are never exposed as Truth.
- R-005 — Same-origin frames and open Shadow DOM may be composed; restricted frames and arbitrary Canvas or WebGL remain explicitly opaque unless an approved semantic bridge supplies revalidatable objects.
- R-006 — Stream gaps and impossible revisions force an exact-tab reset rather than guessed state.

changes.reason: These invariants are consistent across all three current architectural sources.

topics.title: Profile architecture and filtering boundary
topics.summary: Profile behavior and filtering are consistently defined outside control recognition. Profiles may shape Agent-facing behavior and hide controls, but cannot alter control semantics, create authority, or expose protected values.
topics.currentMarkdown:
# Profile architecture

- R-001 — Profiles are strict runtime inputs that contain Agent-facing behavior and bounded filtering policy.
- R-002 — Profile filtering occurs after canonical control recognition and cannot change a control module's recognition or projection semantics.
- R-003 — A filtered control and its action authority are both absent from the Agent projection.
- R-004 — Profile policy cannot reveal editable values, protected values, cookies, browser storage, locators, or arbitrary execution authority.
- R-005 — Profile boundary changes update the normative architecture, observation contract, and decisions together.

changes.reason: The sources state the same separation between canonical semantics and Agent-specific filtering.

topics.title: Legacy migration policy
topics.summary: The migration manifest and component records consistently require reviewed, component-by-component migration from the private legacy archive with provenance, tests, and explicit release limitations. Component migration notes are evidence of bounded imports, not independent product authority.
topics.currentMarkdown:
# Legacy migration policy

- R-001 — Use the private `nanlogic/saccade-legacy` archive only as a reviewed source.
- R-002 — Migrate one approved component at a time; never copy the legacy tree or revive monolithic classifiers.
- R-003 — Every migrated component records its source commit and path, preserves or replaces its focused tests, and retains truthful limitations.
- R-004 — A migration record proves the bounded provenance of that component; it does not independently promote Catalog or public release status.
- R-005 — Public status still requires the current release candidate's browser and evidence gates.

changes.reason: The manifest and all migration notes share the same provenance-first, bounded-component process.

topics.title: Historical Agent and benchmark evidence
topics.summary: The reports are time-scoped evidence from different candidates, clients, sites, and execution routes. Some describe successful same-tab loops while another records a contemporaneous blocker. They should remain historical evidence and must not be merged into a timeless product or performance claim without owner-selected current release evidence.
topics.currentMarkdown:
# Historical Agent evidence policy

- R-001 — Benchmark and dogfood reports are evidence scoped to their recorded candidate, client, browser, task, route, and date.
- R-002 — A local fixture or historical public-site result does not authorize a general compatibility, speed, token, or release claim.
- R-003 — Conflicting pass and blocker reports remain historical until a current frozen matrix supersedes them explicitly.
- R-004 — Current public claims require complete machine-readable evidence from the frozen release candidate.

changes.reason: The reports cover different moments and cannot safely be selected as one timeless current result.
